title: Collections Platform Reference: Extending a Two-Payment Settlement Offer on Own Authority
content:
# Two-Payment Settlement — Extending the Offer

## Scope of the rule

This rule prices a Two-Payment Settlement offer that Ridgeline extends on its own authority on a placed account whose placing agreement is a Starter Contingency Agreement or a Standard Contingency Agreement, the two agreement tiers whose client-tier floor reduction is 0.0; an offer on an account placed under any other agreement tier is outside this rule and stays under the base floor rule.

Ridgeline extends the Two-Payment offer on its own authority at exactly the Two-Payment offer percentage, never at another percentage.

A Two-Payment offer is never a Hardship Settlement, so no hardship hold is needed to extend it.

The Two-Payment Settlement is a programme of Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements; the request it answers is a consumer's request to settle one placed account in two settlement payments.

## What the platform action does

`issue_two_payment_settlement_offer_a21e4b5c` extends a written Two-Payment Settlement offer on one placed account on Ridgeline's own authority. One call opens a new settlement for the account in status offered, dated today, under the Two-Payment Settlement programme: two settlement payments 30 calendar days apart, the first falling due 15 calendar days after today if the consumer accepted today, and the offer open for acceptance through the 30th calendar day after today. The offer records the balance, percentage and amount given, carries no client approval, and books nothing to the settlement balance until it is accepted. The consumer and the agent can see the new offer, with its reference, expiry date and due dates, among the account's settlements.

## How it is invoked

The action is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `issue_two_payment_settlement_offer_a21e4b5c` and then calls it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `account_id` | the Ridgeline account reference number of the placed account the offer would settle, as returned by the placed-account lookup for the verified consumer | identifier |
| `balance_at_offer` | the account's balance due today, exactly as the placed-account lookup shows it | USD to 2 decimal places, no rounding beyond the cent |
| `settlement_pct` | the settlement percentage offered | percent to 1 decimal place (62.5 means 62.5 percent of the balance) |
| `settlement_amount` | the amount that settles the account in full | USD to 2 decimal places; stored as given, rounded only to the cent |
| `bundle_applied` | whether the offer is part of a same-client bundle | enum: `true` — extended as part of a bundle covering the consumer's accounts under one client agreement, with the bundle reduction in its percentage; `false` — the offer stands alone without any bundle reduction |

## Return

A text rendering of a dictionary with: `settlement_id` (the new settlement reference); `status` (always "offered" on success); `variant_name` ("Two-Payment Settlement"); `offer_date` and `offer_expiry_date` (YYYY-MM-DD); `settlement_pct` (percent, 1 decimal); `settlement_amount` (USD, 2 decimals); `payment_count` (integer 2); `first_payment_due_date` and `final_payment_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, assuming acceptance today); `bundle_applied` (true or false). A returned `settlement_id` means the offer was recorded.

## Hypothetical input and receipt

Called with a hypothetical account reference, balance, percentage and amount and `bundle_applied` true, the receipt echoes the percentage and amount given and shows status offered, variant Two-Payment Settlement, payment count 2, an expiry date 30 days after today and a first due date 15 days after today.
